question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{y\sqrt{x}}{9}, & 0\le x\le 9,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

The marginal CDF ${F}_{Y}(y)$ of $Y$ is given by

$$
{F}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & y<0 \\ g(y), & 0\le y\le 1 \\ 1 & y>1.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the function $g(y)?$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{9}\frac{y\sqrt{x}}{9}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{y}{9}{\int }_{0}^{9}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{y}{9}{[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3/2}]}_{x=0}^{x=9} \\  & =\frac{2y}{27}{[{x}^{3/2}]}_{x=0}^{x=9} \\  & =\frac{2y}{27}({9}^{3/2}-{0}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{2y}{27}(27-0) \\  & =2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the marginal CDF of $Y$ for $0\le y\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{y}{f}_{Y}(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{y}2u\,\text{d}u \\  & ={[{u}^{2}]}_{0}^{y} \\  & ={y}^{2}-0 \\  & ={y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${F}_{Y}(y)$ is

$$
{F}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & y<0 \\ {y}^{2}, & 0\le y\le 1 \\ 1 & y>1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $g(y)={y}^{2}.$
